1.explanation:
• monitorAdapter (in src/lib/monitor-adapter.js) should be pulling the VM’s slider metadata (min, max, step) off of an imported/created monitor and passing it through into the React props. If it only maps label, value, etc., then any custom range is lost and the defaults (0–100) prevail.  
• SliderMonitor (in src/components/monitor/slider-monitor.jsx) currently has hard-coded defaultProps {min: 0, max: 100, isDiscrete: true}, and its <input> always uses those props if none are supplied. To honor custom ranges, the defaults must be removed or overridden by incoming props.  
• The SliderMonitor container (src/containers/slider-monitor.jsx) spreads only its own props into the component (mainly value and onSliderUpdate) and doesn’t pump through min, max, or step. It needs to accept and forward custom range props from its parent.  
• Monitor.handleSetModeToSlider (in src/containers/monitor.jsx) flips the mode to “slider” when the user clicks that control, but there is no accompanying dialog logic or propagation of range values. That class will need to hook up a right-click (context menu) handler, open a “Slider Range” dialog, write back the new min/max into the VM, and then round-trip those values through monitorAdapter into the slider component.
1.bug_scenario: The user is right-clicking on a slider monitor in Scratch 3.0 expecting to be able to change its min/max range (as they can in Scratch 2.0), but newly created slider monitors in 3.0 always default to 0–100. Even when importing a 2.0 project that had custom slider ranges, those ranges are not being applied in 3.0.—the slider track and dialog always show min 0 and max 100.

2.explanation:
1. src/lib/monitor-adapter.js: This adapter is responsible for reading the VM’s monitor metadata and turning it into props (min, max, isDiscrete, etc.) for the React monitor components. It currently doesn’t surface custom min/max values from imported projects.

2. src/components/monitor/slider-monitor.jsx: The SliderMonitor component implements the HTML <input type="range"> and uses defaultProps to force min=0 and max=100 whenever props.min or props.max are missing. Even if the dialog captures new values, they never reach this component without the adapter mapping them.

3. src/containers/slider-monitor.jsx: This container wraps SliderMonitorComponent, wires up value changes (handleSliderUpdate), and spreads incoming props (including min/max) into the presentation component. If monitorAdapter doesn’t supply min/max, the container has nothing to pass through.

Fixing the bug requires: 1) extending monitorAdapter to extract and pass any saved/custom slider range from the VM’s monitor object; 2) ensuring that src/containers/slider-monitor.jsx receives and forwards those props; 3) removing or modifying the hardcoded defaultProps in SliderMonitor so that it respects incoming props.min and props.max rather than always falling back to 0–100.
2.bug_scenario: The screenshots show a slider monitor in Scratch 3.0 defaulting to a 0–100 range—even when opening the “Slider Range” dialog (via right-click) on an imported Scratch 2.0 project that had a custom range. The modal correctly presents Min/Max inputs, but the actual slider monitor stays fixed at 0–100.
